svg.aria-label: How the library samples __TEXT pages and compares two snapshots of their residency to tell a cold launch from a warm one

g.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Telling a cold launch from a warm one
The library samples the app's code pages, then compares their residency before main() with their residency when the app becomes active.
code, read-only: the kernel discards and re-reads these pages
writable, so residency says nothing about the launch
Up to 256 pages, spaced evenly through the __TEXT segments of every image in the app's bundle.
The demo app has 413 samplable pages, so the sample covers 62% of them. A system app's median is 6, which the sample covers whole.
A cold launch reads all four segments from disk. The sample covers __TEXT alone, because the measured thresholds are a property of its pages.
Each cell stands for about 6 of the 256 sampled pages, sorted by when the page became resident. Both launches end with the same 240 pages resident; only the split moves.
The ratio never reaches 1, because some pages were already resident when the constructor ran. Measured on an iPhone 16 Pro Max: 0.70 to 0.72 after a reboot, at most 0.03 warm.
The page counts illustrate those measured ratios rather than reproducing one launch. Segment widths are not to scale.
